title: Tyson Bagent, Zavion Thomas on Bears' 24-15 preseason victory vs. Titans | Press Conference
text: What' you see on the first play when they bring up with Stroga and Xav? >> Yeah, I saw the safety come down to the boundary. We had mere double double move concepts on that on each side. Um safety came down um little mishap in the protection adjustment that we made, but you know, obviously get being able to get the ball up gives Avon a chance and then you're able to see that speed uh after that, which is, you know, big reason why he's here. >> Was he where you just like this touchdown? Yeah, I thought I would have been very surprised uh if he got tackled. >> You guys always talk about starting fast, especially on offense. How big of a boost is it when you throw a 97 yard touchdown pass first play? >> Um yeah, it's a huge boost. I don't know that I've thrown a touchdown um of that many yards and I I think that was Zavon Thomas's very first play in the NFL. So, greatest start in NFL history. Um yeah, huge confident boost. I mean, that was the focal point, you know, as I didn't get to play last week, but coming off of the week, the first week, the first preseason game, uh, the focal point for for myself, uh, was to, you know, not go three and out two consecutive times. So, being able to get it get off to a good start, um, good execution, uh, being able to overcome penalties early on, uh, I thought that that was, uh, I thought I thought we were able to move in the right direction. Obviously, you have confident already, but a play like that has got to give you, I would imagine, a level of confidence coming into the game as opposed you don't even think about it anymore. >> Yeah, I think you you you know, you always like to rip the band-aid off some point in the game, whether that be, you know, get touched a little bit, get a get a good completion. Uh, you know, maybe not 97 yards, but, you know, of some sort just to, you know, see yourself throw the ball to a guy, see him catch it. Um, so to be able to start off like that, I think it's just able to give the entire team energy, you know, going on for the rest of the game. >> I sense a fine line between confidence and cockiness. Where do you think Xavon is right now? >> Yeah, I think that he knows what's ahead for him. Um, this is no easy ride being in the NFL, no matter what position you are, no matter how fast you are. So, I think he has a good understanding of there's a lot of work uh to be done, but it's also good to to have success early on. So, you know, because he is fast, so you got a fast guy with confidence. Um I I don't think that's a bad thing at all, but I think that he's well aware of the workload that that is ahead for him. >> On the fly sweep, is that just a matter of him squeezing it or >> Yeah, I mean we can we'll go ahead and put that one on me. Uh that that you know that can happen. Um obviously got to look at the tape. Um and I think just as a whole got to get better at that. Uh just those plays, those jet sweeps from under center. Um it's been a little bit of a stressor for us in the QB room. So seeing that is obviously not great and obviously something we need to work on going forward. stressor because it's just such a precise time >> just because yeah, you got to have good snap timing and you know, you're not in the gun to where you see a lot of teams do a little pop pass to the guy coming in motion. You can't see necessarily where he's at or how fast he's moving and he's in a condensed split. So, nothing that we can't handle. I don't want to talk about it too much, but obviously something that we can get better at going into week one. >> The fourth downs, it seemed like you guys were really confident um in those situations tonight. Was that just a boost for you personally? Yeah, I think it would obviously you convert on fourth down and that's huge for the big boys up front. I know the first one was a pass, but I think that second one being able to um being able to convert short yardage run uh when pretty much everybody in the stadium knows you're running the ball. I think that that's a huge confident boost for the big boys. Uh as far as where the how the success happened, I would say it's a mixture of uh good play calls, especially on that first one. That wasn't something that we necessarily had on the call sheet. So Ben being able to, you know, pull that out of his bag, being able to communicate it in the huddle and to have good execution on something that wasn't necessarily on the call sheet. Um, I thought that that was also a huge confident boost for the skill guys. >> At this point last year, you guys were probably still trying to absorb a lot of Ben's and digest a lot of Ben's system. How do you feel uh teamwide uh about your readiness for week one? Yeah, I mean we've I've kind of answered this question a bunch um this this off seasonason and it's just like you know being able to bathe in the same language for a consecutive year. I think we've been able to see it uh and compare you know last year in the springtime to this year in the springtime, last year's fall camp to this year's fall camp. We we've been able to look at both of those and obviously see uh the comfortability go up with plays being called and the execution as well go up. uh and being able to peel back the layers into you know 303 404 would just because everybody has such a good understanding um from a base level of what we are trying to do as an offense. >> Couple more >> Maurice was just telling me uh that you and he put in extra work in the offseason. Uh, and you know, he continues to put good things on tape. title: Todd Monken Press Conference | August 29th, 2026
text: Obviously, every day is an evaluation and all that stuff, but how much is a day like today, how much can it kind of weigh in, you know, keep, you know, in terms of final decisions? >> Some, but not much. I mean, at this point, you know, your body of work is what it is. We just want to get a good practice in today. >> So, do you expect Joe Lawyer to make the team? >> What's that? >> Do you expect Joe Lawyer to make the team this year? >> Oh, I'm not going to comment on that. >> We talked to Carson before. Um, what was the issue that was that kept him out for that three weeks or so? >> Again, that's a medical. I I really don't want to speak to anything medically. >> And then, do you feel like he was saying saying he's ready to go, he feels back. Um, how comforting is it to have him back with some time before week one to kind of regain his steady footing? >> No, and that was the plan. That was the plan. Uh, with what he was dealing with, hey, let's take it slow with it, and then just get you back with a couple of weeks before we play. >> Todd, you guys you guys played Carson earlier in the year last year, and then again kind of later in the year. What did you What did you see from him game planning for him or just watching him? >> He just kind of grows on you. I mean, just the way he plays the game, the way he sees it, he's decisive, right? Like, once he pulls the trigger, I mean, he he goes, you know, he's just, uh, fantastic athlete that once he, like said, he does a great job during the week of anticipating, you know, what you're going to do offensively, and this defense I think fits him like a glove, allows him to run and hit. >> Todd, on a day like today, obviously, you have a lot of your decisions made, but there are some difficult ones, too. What is your approach, uh, as they're kind of wrapping up and you're making those final decisions on how guys leave this building? >> Well, I said it after the game. I got a lot of respect for NFL players, especially during training camp. When you walk in the door every day and you're competing for a job, right? The majority of your players. Yeah, there's certain players that are going to be here, but the rest of them that are comp- have to compete every day. So, it is hard. It is hard to make those decisions and to let guys go, but it's the nature of the beast. We can't keep everybody. And I've been really proud of the way our guys have practiced from the moment I've gotten here and the way they've they've worked. >> What have you learned most about your team Todd, since from the start even the off-season program to this to this point? >> Oh, I've said it lots of times. I mean, our guys they're a fun group to be around. I mean, they are a fun group to be around. Personality-wise, right? As people, but more importantly, how they work. Like you rarely have to say anything to the guys and you just say it to them once and then they respond, which makes it fun to be around every day. >> There's a few guys like Mike Burton is one who hasn't had a lot of practice time or a game. So, how much of weighing those roster statuses are just projection? >> Some of it, other than we had Mike for a couple practices last week. He got in there a little bit and he just picked up where he left off. I mean, a guy that's played fullback for his whole career and has gotten this far along like uh it was as if he never practiced It was as if he never missed a day. I mean, it was uh it was really really fun to watch. >> player, you can give a little more. >> I think so. I think that's that's exactly right. Guys that you've seen it before and then you just get them back on the field. It's a little easier cuz you've already seen it. That's a good point. Yes. >> When you watch the film of you and Jaylen after that game, did you come away from it uh assured that you and Andrew have to have healthy debate over this. Did you come away knowing what you would want to do in that situation or are you still grappling with it, or how's this going to turn out? >> Somewhat. I mean, like a lot of players, we don't want to lose any good players that have a future with the Browns. So, we've got still have some discussions to have, but I I was very impressed with Dylan and Taylen. Uh both did it differently, but you know, Dylan's at least played uh he's played last year. He's gotten more reps than Taylen, so he looked like it. And we had you know, he he obviously operated very well, and then Taylen did the things we thought he would do, which was make some plays with his feet. And there was no issues in terms of the operation. The issues we had were a bobbled snap on a fly sweep that we almost lost, and then a fumbled snap, and that was really with Dylan. Outside of that, our operation was really clean with those guys. So, that's what you're looking for. >> The week leading up to the season are are you approached that you like to start working on Jacksonville immediately, or do you wait until that week arrives? >> Earlier Earlier in the Earlier in the week will be a little bit more of us versus us, and as we get to the middle and back end of the week, there'll be more and more Jacksonville. By the last day, by Thursday, it'll be all Jacksonville. >> Todd, what what have you thought of Boston Barber in these last 2 weeks playing right guard? >> What a great job he's done playing starting at tackle, then going to guard, and I think he's only going to continue continue to get better. Uh so, uh been very pleased with him. He takes coaching. There was a screen that we ran during the game that the week before uh when it got caught, he was a little bit casual down the field, not accelerating his feet, and you saw it in the game the other night, he accelerated, and ran through the defender to get out the way on the defender and and did a great job. So, he certainly takes coaching uh from the meeting room from his past experiences to the field. >> You said Evanston looks better at tackle. >> He does. >> Does Barber look better at guard than tackle? Can you make any observation about that? >> Um I don't know if he looks better there. I would just say we were pleasantly surprised once we moved him there that he didn't look out of place. So, that part of it I wouldn't know if he looked better, but um he certainly looked looked you know, certainly very capable. >> Is that position settled with Tevin or could Austin still kind of make a push there? >> I Again, I I love our depth there. Again, I think that Tevin has the advantage, obviously, he's being the veteran player, but we still have this week. We still have today and a few practices to really kind of finalize. Um I would give Tevin the lean, but I don't think it's it's done yet. >> When you look at Tevin Who is When you look at corner and tight end, those feel like a couple spots where you That was about injuries, could be depth concerns. Are those spots where you think that could continue to change even after Sunday, right? You could have some new guys coming in or will need to have some new guys perhaps coming in? >> I think it's possible. I don't think there's any position on your team minus a few that you're not always looking to upgrade. Should a player become available that gives you an opportunity to upgrade your roster. >> Todd, with a a veteran like Derek coming in late, you know, what's the process of sort of getting them, you know, acclimated and and up to speed and where you you feel comfortable putting, you know, getting them out there and and playing? >> Well, again, he's played in this this style of defense. We're talking about Derek Barnett, right? Is that who we're talking about? >> Yeah. >> Yeah, so he's played in this style of defense. I mean, so it's not that big of a transition, right? It's It's really not. It's It's really just getting used to what we call things, our terminology, but and then just seeing what we have. I mean, we haven't been around Derek and I've liked what I've seen so far. >> Have you and the defensive coaches made a decision on Michael Hall going forward >> Have not. I mean, I I think he's shown that he can be a versatile player. I do think he's more disruptive So, I do think that. He has shown that. We have seen that on tape. I think that would probably be at this point. We still have another week to go through. It would be the starting point with some defensive end flex. >> And you mentioned Calvin in the O-line. Have you seen as the five group of five who's just started to practice more and more? Can you see the chemistry building and that they're taking the steps that you need them to take before you get to the season? >> Sure. No, I think the more that they work together, communicate together, run the same concepts and schemes, right? I think you're just going to continue to see them uh grow. >> When you take into consideration whether you would go Barber or Jenkins over there, do you think about the fact that that would give you two rookies, you know, starting on the line or do you just take each guy for his own merit? >> It's really just trying to put the best five out there. At some point, you're like, well, would it be ideal to have 11 rookies starting? Of course not, right? But ultimately, our job is to put the best 11 out there, whether it's a rookie or a vet. And if that turns out to be Austin, then great. If it's Tevaughn, then great. >> Todd, coming back to to Thursday night, you you you had Kingsley go first with both quarterbacks and then Luke come in. What was sort of the thinking behind, you know, kind of the the center rotation? >> Just giving them opportunities with each quarterback. You know, whether one starts or one plays in the second quarter, some of it is you know, you're you're also getting into possible two-minute scenarios, which are only going to come up in the second and fourth quarter that you want to see maybe with different players uh at every position. So, it really wasn't anything other than we had planned on dividing up uh try to divide up the reps with those guys. >> The The games are really the only way to evaluate your special teams cuz you can't go >> Mhm. >> What are your observations about what your special teams coordinator has done first I can I can go by how we practice and the time that we utilize in terms of our drill work and what I see. And I've been highly impressed at our coaching and our work that we've put in and it's shown up on on tape, which is what you want to see from your coaching, right? The drills that you're doing have to show up on tape or you're doing the wrong drills. Everybody says that and it's true. Like, what are we doing? And then once it isn't where we want it to be, how do we fight like hell to fix it and drill it differently so our guys really understand? I've seen that carry over. I've seen it in all phases. So, I'm excited about that. And you're right, we really won't know in all the phases till we really start playing uh meaningful games, but I've been impressed so far at whoever's been out there at their execution. >> Any concerns then on using K.C. Keeler as a as a punt returner that he looked so good in that Bears game since he's been getting a lot of time at receiver? >> Sure. No, I mean, but to me, I look at punt return as an opportunity for an explosive, right? In terms of changing field position. So, you do have to balance that. I think you do have to balance the risk of that, but at this point, it makes too much sense. It makes too much sense for us to use him in every way we can as a weapon. And that's one of those. >> With Joe Last one here. >> With Joe Williams not being here, does it change at all your philosophy in terms of more 11 personnel, less 12, or were you going to do what you're going to do anyway? >> Well, it's hard to say. It's It has nothing to do with Joe. I mean, Joe hasn't been with us, you know, really all of training camp. So, it really has to do with who's in the room as much as anything. Would we feel as comfortable in 21 personnel without Mike? Right now that Mike's back, how would we feel? We don't know how the roster's going to look offensively here in two or three days. Who do we have, right? What are the pieces that we have? I've been really impressed with Harold and his diligence in becoming a better blocker along with Blake. I've seen some guys that have really took a step forward in terms of uh the point of attack and also as a C-gap blocker. So, I feel like we'll see where we're at as we move further in the next couple of days, but I feel pretty good about our ability to use all the personnel groupings that we have. All right, thank you.

title: Carson Schwesinger Press Conference | August 29th, 2026
text: What can you tell us about what's kept you out? You've been out for 3 weeks. >> I mean, it's just football. Sometimes things happen and and you got to try and be smart about it. It's basically it. I'm ready to roll now. >> Are you ready? >> Yeah, I'll be out there today. >> So, how frustrating was that for you? >> Uh yeah, it's pretty frustrating. Um it's cool also to be able to watch uh the guys. I think seeing what what Easton was able to do and get in there and run the show was pretty cool. Um especially since we came came in together and we basically learned this defense together. Um and I think just the the hard part was trying to just be able to stay mentally locked in every day and still find ways to learn and and get better um even though you're not getting those reps out on the field. >> So, even though your defense has worked this year you get better by practicing. What How can you catch up physically rather than mentally? >> Yeah, I think well, uh I mean, physically it's just getting the body back ready to roll. I mean, uh at the end of the day it's just being being wanting to go out there and and run to the ball again when I'm out there and and get the body back in shape. So, I'm not too worried about that and um like I said, I think uh big thing for me was making sure the mental's there the whole time and so uh just hit the ground running with that. >> Do you view it as a setback at all that you weren't able to be out there for a couple >> No. Um you know, obviously, you if if I could have, I would have wished to not miss them, but um still tried to to go in every day and and and find ways to get better uh in other ways and and get ready to roll. >> And nothing that's going to linger and you're not worried about it. >> No. >> What did you see by watching? >> What do you mean? >> About your defense. What did >> I think we learned a lot over camp. Um I think we got got a lot better. We I mean, that's the whole point of practice, right? I mean, we we were able to uh hammer a bunch of things down on the back end on the front and and I mean, going against the the offense that we have, they basically throw everything at you that you could possibly see and so um we were able to to get a ton of looks that that you don't normally see and uh we were able to learn from them and and you know, get ready and and really hammer everything out. >> Carson, you look like you're on the cage chomping at the bit to get back in. Well, that's why we have a great training staff and great coaches that obviously are there to protect us and and in some cases protect us from ourselves. So, yeah, I'm ready to get back out there and I mean they know the thing with me is when I'm out there I'm going 100%. So, we've obviously checked everything we need to so that I'm able to do that. I mean, yeah, without a draft process you you get a lot more rest. I think that was a big one is getting the body back healthy. So, that was that was big and then just there's there's less stress of the whole draft process and so you can focus more on on getting getting better, getting stronger, faster and and really getting mentally prepared too as well. Yeah, I think there was some peace of mind with that. I didn't know it was any later. I think just we we we looked at the schedule and and mapped it out and at the end of the day I'm I'm excited to be back and go practice again and and not have to sit and watch. I think a lot of what we preach on the defense is that is the ball's our oxygen and you need oxygen to breathe. So, every play obviously you have your assignment, your alignment, your technique, but at the end of the day you got to be thinking about the ball and going and getting the ball and that that stems from that mindset is all those turnovers. Yeah, I mean yeah, that's the I mean we you can see that it's on guys' minds. I mean, that's what happens when you preach that type of mindset is is it gets drilled in and when when guys are out there it doesn't matter. Maybe you miss your assignment all this but at the end of the day at the end of the play all you got to be thinking about is the ball. So, getting to the ball, running there, punching out, getting getting tips, getting overthrows, everything like that. >> How would you say the personality of the defense has changed with Jared Davis and and like a rookie too? >> I think both those guys have come in and really made an impact. I think vocally they're two guys that we can lean on. Quincy obviously having all the experience. We made fun of him today cuz he turned 30 yesterday. So, just his experience is is huge and then same with Jared having a guy who can come in and and obviously lead by example but also be able to you know get us going too as well as is big and you know their impact on the field is huge. >> Carson, what can you do to improve on your rookie of the year season? >> A lot. There's I mean every aspect of the game you want to talk about. Getting better at stopping the run, getting better at seeing the formations before the ball snap, better at dropping in coverage, rushing the passer. I think you know every area of my game has room to improve and that's what I'm trying to do this year. >> Okay Carson, with without Miles here obviously that's a big change, right? Um, how do you think offenses are going to approach you schematically differently? It felt like last year things were kind of tilted away from him. Do you think it'll be more balanced this year? >> I mean you could see some. I think with our front you get attacked very similarly just because of how our our front four play. So, obviously you might see some changes or or more runs go to both sides and things like that but you know at the end of the day we we put our 11 out there and and our whole goal is to to cause chaos on on the offensive side of the ball and and make plays. >> Since you observe everything out there while watching, what what do you think about the offense this year? What's the biggest difference that you're practicing >> I think I mean totally new offense to go against for us. I mean we went went against it twice when we played Baltimore last year, but just able to see that that really everything's available. I think there's a lot that they can do. I think we have, you know, the the receiver position has gained a lot of dynamic players, which defensively is is something that you always have to account for and same thing on the O-line. And so I'm I'm ready, you know, as as a defense we go get the ball back to the offense and they're going to put some points on the board. >> You mentioned Easton before. How have you seen him kind of develop? It looked like last year he was a guy that you know whatever, undrafted guy and now this year he took takes your spot, he's calling the signals all this stuff. >> Yeah, I think just just the confidence he has when he steps on the field has been huge. It's not It's not easy to go out there and call the plays and and and run the show defensively. And so him being able to go out there and really there's not there wasn't a step lost. I mean, the the control of the defense and and being able to get all the calls and everything like that and then just to the the effort to the ball. I mean, you can really see it with him. You saw it on on on the interception 2 days ago. At the end of the day to him the ball's oxygen. >> How have you guys responded taken to Mike Vrabel? I know how much you guys loved Jim Schwartz, but how has >> I love having Vrabel here. I think I've already learned a lot from him. I'm excited to to get into the year now and I was excited to practice all camp. So now I'm excited to practice today and really get that going and and get our connection on the field going as well, you know, just as we have off the field. >> Whenever I asked coach Munchak about you, he kept saying we're really cautious, we're really cautious. If we were in the regular season, how much time would you have missed? >> I mean, you could I might have a different answer than the trainers. I I could tell you that I could have a broken leg and I'd still play. So that's what I'd say. >> But you talked about without giving any trade secrets, but like what did >> Uh I mean, it's it's really everything. I mean, um football is one of the the few sports where you can't practice as much as you'd like. We have 16 games, and even in practice, you can never go live and everything. And so, really there's an edge you can gain to to being able to go out there and watch film and and take everything in from that. Some of it And it's just watching a lot of stuff like that and um you know, formation a lot of pre-snap stuff, all motions, how they come out the huddle, things like that. And and really you can just through watching it a lot, you can pick things up. >> Thanks, Brandon. >> Yeah, thank you. >> Thanks, Brandon. Last question. >> Yeah.

title: Tytus Howard Press Conference | August 29th, 2026
text: Um How much is the last week or so now that you guys have sort of solidified that first group, how much have you seen a benefit just on the field in communication, cohesion, that sort of thing? >> Yeah, the camaraderie is is going up. Now, we we're getting a lot of repetition with a lot of the same guys. Uh we getting a chance to get a feel for everyone's game. It's been better for us in a run and pass uh for the past week or two. Protection has went up a lot. We got a lot better. I mean, that showed in the game. But, offensive line grew to the same game cuz those guys been working together every day, too. So, it's been a lot better. >> How I mean, we talk so much about that chemistry. How hard is that to build, you know, when you have a bunch of new guys, but basically a whole new starting five? How tough is that to build? >> I mean, it's a it's the group on the field that always got to be on the same page. Um all five guys got to be on the same page at all times uh cuz if one person busts protection, run play, that can be the that can mess up the whole play. So, being able to get all those reps together and be able to be on the same page, especially like you said with five brand new guys, um you know, it's tough, but that's something we've been working through the whole camp. And we lately we've been getting a lot more reps together. So, it's getting better and better. >> Specifically with the guy right you know, that right guard spot's been the something that's been a you know, just a constant rotation. >> Mhm. >> With Kevin there, you know, specifically with him, how important is it to to really kind of get to know and that that guy that that's to your immediate left? >> Oh, man, it's been phenomenal. To get a chance to play beside Tevin, Tevin's got better every single week he's been here, ever since I've been here. And uh all the all the work he's put in this off season to get to the point he's at right now, I'm excited to see what he's able to do this year. Like I said, um anything he need from me, you know, that I can help him, just let me know. And like whether it's after practice or what, getting extra reps in. But, I feel like Teven's done a really good job of solidifying himself on the right side and you know, looking forward to playing next to him. >> Austin Bar has been getting a lot of work at guard. So, what what have you seen when you're watching the film of him these last couple of weeks and and seeing that transition for him? >> Baller. Uh start off the right tackle, he played right tackle, right guard, uh moved a little bit on the left side, left tackle, uh left guard also, um and he can play all what, four positions everything but center, so him being able to get all that repetition early on in his career, uh it's going to help him out a lot. He's going to slow the game down for him I know for sure cuz I've done that and being able to know what to do at every single position uh when you get out you're going to you're going to be able to play faster, you know, and it's going to only get him better technically which uh I seen this past week he did right guard, he played really well and what the past 2 weeks. So, it's only going to make him better, but Austin's got a bright future ahead of him, whether it's at guard or tackle. >> You guys have held so many like run fit sessions all summer long. What have you learned from those that you guys will be able to do in the run game as an offensive line and what have you learned that you need to work on as you as the regular season approaches? >> I say the biggest thing is we got a big offensive line, so we got a lot of big We do it correctly, we do our technique the right way, we fit the double teams like we were able to fit, nobody's going to be able to stay in front of us. We're going to be able to move anybody out the way. It's just a matter of like you said, being consistent every play with the technique that coach Warharness teaching, uh being dialed into snap count, everybody getting off the ball at the same time and I think that's the biggest thing for us is being dialed in on snap count, being consistent every play. We take those steps of getting better each week, sky's the limit. >> What how difficult are these these couple of days as, you know, guys you've been you know, you've been working with working alongside, you know, for months, you know, the uncertainty that kind of hangs over it, you know, guys' careers, you know, dreams can can kind of How tough is it and what do you do to try to maybe help some of the guys that, you know, kind of get through those, you know, kind of those uncertain times? >> Yeah, it's definitely a tough time of year, man. You see guys out here fighting for their families, fighting for their livelihood, putting in the work each and every day. You got guys that, you know, go as hard as possible, like even harder than guys who going to know they're going to make the team and you to see those guys not make it is definitely a tough situation, but, you know, I think the good thing about being here is a lot of the guys put in a lot of good work and so them being able to showcase some of the film they had this preseason, other teams being able to look at it, so they're hopeful that, you know, another team might see, "Hey, I seen how this guy performed for the Browns, so I will go ahead and give him a chance." Or, you know, they can come back on the practice squad or or whatever it may seem, but I know as far as offensive line, what I try to do every year is, you know, with days like this coming up, I try to get the guys together, you know, have a big dinner, you know, kind of like a last supper with all of us cuz, you know, the group's not going to be the same as it was all camp, so being able to get that relationship with guys out the field is a big, you know, big key. >> What what have you learned about Dontrell Hilliard as a runner here? Just kind of getting into this. Yeah, I know it's hard with, you know, you can't tackle him and stuff like that, but what have you learned about >> I mean, the biggest thing I'll take away from Dontrell Hilliard's game is he he's very physical. Um as you can see, some of the clips, run, pass, chipping D ends, like like Q is physical, like everything about his game is physical and that fits into the mold of what we trying to be as a offense. The line, we trying to be physical every single play. Um because if we can be physical every play and get the running game going with Q, it's going to open up the game, make it easier for, you know, Deshaun back there quarterback to see the field, you know, have a lot of space to throw the ball and like I said, it's going to start with us in the running game first. >> Do you kind of like blocking for a back like that that can kind of match your guys' physicality? >> Oh, yeah, for sure, man. I've been a fan of of Q since he was in high school. He's from Montgomery, Alabama. My mom lives in from lives in Montgomery. I'm from that area, too. So, you know, I've been a fan of his game from when he went there, the Ole Miss, back to Ohio State. I know what type of player he is and I I know what to expect from him on Sundays. >> Tytus, the last time we talked to you was earlier this Monday. This is the first time you've played since you've been here. And one big takeaway for us to see you with during the joint practice last week was hopefully you would be in a better position in the joint practice. And what were some things you were really impressed with from our younger peers on the offensive line going against a playoff caliber D-line like that? >> Uh, I mean, if I'm being honest, I feel like we blocked those guys extremely well in joint practice. Uh, you know, obviously going to be a couple plays uh in the practice, but I feel like as a group we stood up to those guys and we blocked them really well. And I I was really impressed with the way we competed. Uh, like you said, versus a caliber of playoff caliber team, uh the Bills are going to be a deep playoff team every year, you know, one of the best teams in the league. And I feel like us as a uh organization we're trying to get to where they at right now. And I think that was a good start. >> You've been you've been in the NFL for a couple years, but do you recall walking away from joint practice feeling like that about yourself and the offensive line after going to joint practices like that? >> Yeah, I I I like I've been in plenty of joint practices and, you know, to go against the B here and then go against a team like that in a joint practice and walk away feeling like we felt last week like, "Hey, we can compete with anyone." with the way we practice, you know, it's pretty impressive. So, I'm looking forward to seeing what we do the first game against Jacksonville. Like you said, it's another playoff team. And that was a good warm-up for that game. >> Tytus, I know you you played with Derek in in Houston. Can you talk about what he can bring to the table for this team? >> Oh, you're talking D.B.? Yeah. Yeah, Barnett, he's a a feisty player, really good player, can play uh on both sides at end. Uh, which is a guy that's going to be able to get to the quarterback. Uh, going to play hard. Um, you know, D.B. and D.B. been going against each other for the past 2 and 1/2 years at practice. Uh, and to see the type of plays he made when he came in in Houston with limited amount of snaps. Uh, so I'm excited to see what he can do here when he's going to be getting more snaps here. so uh he's a good good player. I know he's going to do good things for Browns. Yep. >> Thank you. Thank you.

title: Derek Barnett Press Conference | August 29th, 2026
text: What's one of your early impressions of this team been since joining? >> Uh it's been moving fast. I think we have a great team. Uh I think we've got a great opportunity this year to play some good football and put our best foot forward. >> Jared, how much did having a couple guys back in the Houston that are in this game? How much of that kind of help maybe the decision or just kind of give you some info on the team before officially, you know, kind of committing to one so? >> Yeah, I think it's always good when you go to a team when you play with a couple guys. If you play in the league long enough, you you cross paths with a lot of guys you played with or even coaches or trainers. Um sometimes even equipment guys, too. So, it's always good to know somebody like when you go to a new program. >> I think you were working when the Eagles won the Super Bowl. >> Yeah, long time ago. >> Yeah. So, Schwartz was there. He had still this defense. Does it look the same at least up front to you as what you remember? >> Yeah, up front it's a lot of the same as it's just some different lingo things. So, just different language. Um but I think for the most part it's it's some similarities. >> Just from an objective minded standpoint with this defense, do you feel like from a production standpoint, do you see, you know, good big things for yourself this year? >> Uh yeah, I mean every year that's what you want as a as a, you know, competitor. Um but at the end of the day, it's all about winning. And so, you do want to play well in every game. Um you know, every game's not going to be perfect, but the main thing is just winning. >> What was that process like for you in the off-season, I guess, by not knowing where you're going to be and kind of the wait in the training camp before you find a spot? >> Yeah, um it was a little different this year, but I was just trying to practice patience and I knew eventually something would come come come about. Um so, I was just trying to be patient in the process and not get too ahead of myself. >> A young guy like Jared Verse has talked a lot about sort of craving that veteran mentorship and having someone show him the way. Is that something you pride yourself on is kind of helping out those young guys and are are you eager to help Jared? >> Yeah, I'm always uh trying to be a help to anybody, you know, but uh like also like I can learn from a young guy, too, you know? I think uh you can play 1 year 10 years in this league. Um like the day you stop trying to learn and get better, that's when you kind of hit a wall and I think in this business you always trying to get better and learn as players and coaches. >> How much do you think >> I was going to follow up on that real quick. What do you know about Jared's game? Have you seen much of him and just what do you think of him as as a rusher? >> Yeah, I watched a lot of uh Jared's game, you know, just breaking down film throughout the week. Um I mean, you're in the building 18 plus weeks, so you watch you lot watch a lot of guys' tapes um just leading up to other games. And I think he's a great player. Um I mean, I don't really I don't really have to say much about him. Like he's made a lot of plays in this league already. He's just He's still a young player, so uh I just think he has to just keep continuing his craft and just just working his techniques and he has all the talent and tools already. >> How much do you think coming in, you know, when you did, you know, maybe little less fewer hits on you through the course of the preseason, how much does that kind of help you be a little more fresh, you think, especially early in the early in the season? >> Uh I'm still trying to get up to speed and just every day just trying to get back in football football conditioning, you know? You can run as much as you want, but it's different when you have the helmet and shoulder pads on tugging and pushing on 300 plus pound guys, so you know, just every day just trying to get better and uh get ready for week one. >> La'el Collins was telling us he's thrilled to to have you here. You guys played together, obviously. What What's he like in that defensive line room? >> Uh Maliek, he keeps the room, you know, lax. Uh has a great energy to him. Always clowning joking, but when it's time to work, he he knows how to go. And uh Maliek's he's been doing it for a high level a long time, so I'm excited to work with Maliek again. >> And then with with like him and Jason Garrett, obviously, in the inside, how does that impact you guys as that rush? Does that make it a little easier? >> Yeah, I mean we got two great edge rushers on the inside. I think you just have to elevate your game, you know. Everybody's trying to get home and make big plays, so it's just going to push everybody in the room, I think. >> Does the side you rush from matter at all? >> Uh Yeah. wherever. Wherever I can get in at, you know. >> Have you had a chance to go against uh the rookie, Spencer Brown, yet in the past couple times? >> No, I haven't yet. Mhm. >> Good. >> Thank you. >> Cool. Thanks, man. >> Nice to meet y'all. >> Look forward to it.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference | August 29th, 2026
text: Todd, um I would say every day is an evaluation and all that stuff, but how much does a day like today how much can it kind of weigh in, you know, keep, you know, in terms of final decisions and >> Some, but not much. I mean, at this point, you know, uh your body of work is what it is. We just want to get a good practice in today. >> Todd, do you expect Joe Lawyer to make the team this year? >> What's that? >> Do you expect Joe Lawyer to make the team this year? >> Oh, I'm not going to comment on that. >> We talked to Carson before. Um what was the issue that was that kept him out for that three weeks stretch? >> Again, that's a medical. I I really don't want to speak to anything medically. >> And then, do you feel like he was saying saying he's ready to go, he feels back. Um how comforting is it to have him back with some time before week one to kind of regain his step and footing? >> No, and that was the plan. That was the plan uh with what he was dealing with. Hey, let's take it slow with it and then just get you back with a couple weeks before we play. >> Todd, you guys you guys played Carson early in the year last year and then again kind of later in the year. >> Mhm. >> What did you see from him then? >> Game planning for him, just watching him. >> It just kind of grows on you. I mean, it just the way he plays the game, the way he sees it, he's decisive. Right? Like once he pulls the trigger, I mean, he he goes, you know, he's just uh fantastic athlete that once he, like said, he does a great job during the week of anticipating, you know, what you're going to do offensively and this defense I think fits him like a glove, allows him to run and hit. >> Todd, on a day like today, obviously you have a lot of your decisions made, but there are some difficult ones, too. What is your approach uh as they're kind of wrapping up and you're making those final decisions on how guys leave this building? >> Well, I said it after the game. I got a lot of respect for NFL players, especially during training camp. When you walk in the door every day and you're competing for a job, right? The majority of your players. Yeah, there's certain players that are going to be here, but the rest of them that are compact to compete every day. So, it is hard. It is hard to make those decisions and to let guys go, but it's the nature of the beast. We can't keep everybody. And I've been really proud of the way our guys have practiced from the moment I've gotten here and the way they they've worked. >> What have you learned most about your team Todd, since from the start even the off-season program to this to this point? >> Oh, I've said it lots of times. I mean, our guys they're a fun group to be around. I mean, they are a fun group to be around personality-wise, right? As people, but more importantly, how they work. Like, you rarely have to say anything to the guys and you just say it to them once and then they respond, which makes it fun to be around every day. >> There's a few guys like Mike Burton is one who hasn't had a lot of practice time or a game. So, how much of weighing those roster statuses are just projection? >> Some of it, other than we had Mike for a couple practices last week. He got in there a little bit and he just picked up where he left off. I mean, a guy that's played fullback for his whole career and has gotten this far along like uh it was as if he never practiced. It was as if he never missed a day. I mean, it was uh it was really really fun to watch. >> A veteran player, you can give a little more. >> I think so. I think that's that's exactly right. Guys that you've seen it before and then you just get them back on the field. It's a little easier cuz you've already seen it. That's a good point. Yes. >> When you watch the film of you and Andrew after that game, did you come away from it? I'm sure that you and Andrew have to have healthy debate over this. Did you come away knowing what you would want to do in that situation or are you still grappling with it, or how's this going to turn out? >> Somewhat. I mean, like a lot of players, we don't want to lose any good players that have a future with the Browns. So, we've got still have some discussions to have, but I I was very impressed with Dylan and Taylen. Uh both did it differently, but you know, Dylan's at least played uh he's played last year. He's gotten more reps than Taylen, so he looked like it. And we had you know, he he obviously operated very well, and then Taylen did the things we thought he would do, which was make some plays with his feet. And there was no issues in terms of the operation. The issues we had were a bobbled snap on a fly sweep that we almost lost, and then a fumbled snap, and that was really with Dylan. Outside of that, our operation was really clean with those guys. So, that's what you're looking for. >> The week leading up to the season opener are are you a coach that you like to start working on Jacksonville immediately, or do you wait until that week arrives? >> Early >> as far as like >> Early in the Early in the week will be a little bit more of us versus us. And as we get to the middle and back end of the week, there'll be more and more Jacksonville. By the last day, by Thursday, it'll be all Jacksonville. >> Todd, what have you thought of Austin Barber in these last few weeks playing right guard? >> What a great job he's done playing starting at tackle, then going to guard, and I think he's only going to continue continue to get better. Uh so, uh been very pleased with him. He takes coaching. There was a screen that we ran during the game that the week before uh when it got caught, he was a little bit casual down the field, not accelerating his feet, and you saw it in the game the other night, he accelerated, and through the defender to get out the way on the defender and and did a great job. So, he certainly takes coaching uh from the meeting room, from his past experiences to the field. >> You said that Evans and looks better at tackle. >> He does. >> Does Barber look better at guard than tackle? Can you make any observation about that? >> Um I don't know if he looks better there. I would just say we were pleasantly surprised once we moved him there that he didn't look out of place. So, that part of it I wouldn't know if he looked better, but um he certainly looked looked you know, certainly very capable. >> Is that position settled with Teven or could Austin still kind of make a push there? >> I Again, I I love our depth there. Again, I think that Teven has the advantage. Obviously, he's been the veteran player, but we still have this week. We still have today and a few practices to really kind of finalize. Um I would give Teven the lean, but I don't think it's it's done yet. >> Coach, when you look at Coach, when you look at corner and tight end, those feel like a couple spots where you there was a bunch of injuries, could be depth concerns. Are those spots where you think they could continue to change even after Sunday, right? You could have some new guys coming in or will need to have some new guys perhaps coming in? >> I think it's possible. I don't think there's any position on your team minus a few that you're not always looking to upgrade. Should a player become available that gives you an opportunity to upgrade your roster. >> Coach, with a a veteran like Derek comes in late, you know, what's the process of sort of getting them, you know, acclimated and and up to speed and where you you feel comfortable putting, you know, getting them out there and and playing? >> Well, again, he's played in this this style of defense. We're talking about Derek Barnett, right? Is that who we're talking about? Yeah. so he's played in this style of defense. I mean, so it's not that big of a transition, right? It's It's really not. It's It's really just getting used to what we call things, our terminology, but and then just seeing what we have. I mean, we haven't been around Derek, and I've liked what I've seen so far. >> Have you and the defensive coaches made a decision on Michael Hall going forward and or back? >> Have not. I mean, I I think he's shown that he can be a versatile player. I do think he's more disruptive inside. So, I do think that he has shown that. We have seen that on tape. I think that would probably be at this point. We still have another week to go through would be the starting point with some defensive end flex. >> If you mentioned having in the O-line, have you seen as that five group of five has started to practice more and more, can you see the chemistry building and that they're taking the steps that you need them to take before you get to the season? >> Sure. No, I think the more that they work together, communicate together, run the same concepts and schemes, right? I think you're just going to continue to see them grow. >> When you take into consideration whether you would go Barber or Jenkins over there, do you think about the fact that that would give you two rookies, you know, starting on the line, or do you just take each guy for his own merit? >> It's really just trying to put the best five out there. At some point, you're like, well, would it be ideal to have 11 rookies starting? Of course not, right? But ultimately, our job is to put the best 11 out there, whether it's a rookie or a vet. And if that turns out to be Austin, then great. If it's Tevaughn, then great. >> Todd, uh coming back to the Thursday night, you you you had Kingsley do first with both quarterbacks, and then Luke come in. What was sort of the thinking behind, you know, kind of the the center rotation? >> Just giving them opportunities with each quarterback. You know, whether one starts or one plays in the second quarter, some of it is you know, you're you're also getting into possible two-minute scenarios, which are only going to come up in the second, the fourth quarter that you want to see maybe with different players uh at every position. So, it really wasn't anything other than we had planned on dividing up uh try to divide up the reps with those guys. >> The The games are really the only way to evaluate your special teams cuz you can't go >> What are your observations about what your special teams coordinator has done? >> [clears throat] >> first I can I can go by how we practice and the time that we utilize in terms of our drill work and what I see. And I've been highly impressed at our coaching and our work that we've put in and it's shown up on on tape, which is what you want to see from your coaching, right? The drills that you're doing have to show up on tape or you're doing the wrong drills. Everybody says that and it's true. Like, what are we doing? And then once it isn't where we want it to be, how do we fight like hell to fix it and drill it differently so our guys really understand? I've seen that carry over. I've seen it in all phases, so I'm excited about that. And you're right, we really won't know in all the phases till we really start playing uh meaningful games, but I've been impressed so far at whoever's been out there at their execution. >> Any concerns on on using Keke Coutee as a as a punt returner when he's looked so good in that Bears game since he he's getting a lot of time at receiver. >> Sure. No, I mean, but to me I look at punt return as an opportunity for an explosive, right? In terms of changing field position. So, you do have to balance that. I think you do have to balance the risk of that, but at this point it makes too much sense. It makes too much sense for us to use him in every way we can as a weapon, and that's one of those. >> With Joe With Joe Burrow not being here >> With Joe Flacco not being here, does it change at all of your philosophy in terms of more 11 personnel, less 12, or were you going to do what you're going to do anyway? >> Well, it's hard to say. It's It has nothing to do with Joe. I mean Joe hasn't been with us you know, really all of training camp. So, it really has to do with who's in the room as much as anything. Would we feel as comfortable in 21 personnel without Mike? Right? Now that Mike's back, how would we feel? We don't know how the roster is going to look offensively here in 2 or 3 days. Who do we have? Right? What are the pieces that we have? I've been really impressed with Harold and his diligence in becoming a better blocker along with Blake. I've seen some guys that have really took a step forward in terms of the point of attack and also as a C-gap blocker. So, I feel like we'll see where we're at as we move further in the next couple of days, but I feel pretty good about our ability to use all the personnel groupings that we have. >> All right. Thank you. >> All right. Thank you. >> Thank you.

title: Carson Schwesinger Press Conference | August 29th, 2026
text: What can you tell us about what's kept you out? You were out 3 weeks. >> I mean, it's just football. Things happen and and you got to try and be smart about it. It's basically it. I'm ready to roll now. >> Are you ready? >> Yeah, I'll be out there today. >> So, how frustrating was that for you? >> Uh yeah, it's pretty frustrating. Um it's cool also to be able to watch the guys. I think seeing what what Easton was able to do and get in there and run the show was pretty cool. Um especially since we came came in together and we basically learned this defense together. Um and I think just the the hard part was trying to just be able to stay mentally locked in every day and still find ways to learn and and get better even though you're not getting those reps out on the field. >> So, even though you're defensive coordinator you get better by practicing. What how can you catch up physically rather than mentally? >> Yeah, I think well, I mean, physically it's just getting the body back ready to roll. I mean, at the end of the day it's just being being wanting to go out there and and run to the ball again when I'm out there and and get the body back in shape. So, I'm not too worried about that and like I said, I think a big thing for me was making sure the mental's there the whole time and so just hit the ground running with that. >> So, do you view it as a step back at all that you weren't able to be out there for the three weeks? >> No. You know, obviously if if I could have I would have wished to not miss them, but still tried to to go in every day and and find ways to get better in other ways and get ready to roll. >> And nothing that's going to linger in the long run? >> What did you see by watching? >> What do you mean? >> About your defense. What did you >> I think we learned a lot over camp. I think we got got a lot better. We I mean, that's the whole point of practice, right? I mean, we we were able to hammer a bunch of things down on the back end on the front and I mean, going against the the offense that we have they basically throw everything at you that you could possibly see and so we're able to to get a ton of looks that that you don't normally see and we're able to learn from them and and you know get ready and and really hammer everything out. Well, that's why we have a great training staff and great coaches that obviously are there to protect us and and in some cases protect us from ourselves. So, yeah, I'm ready to get back out there and I mean they know the thing with me is when I'm out there I'm going 100% so we've obviously checked everything we need to so that I'm able to do that. I mean yeah, without a draft process you get a lot more rest. I think that was a big one is getting the body back healthy. So, that was that was big and then just there's there's less stress of the whole draft process and so you can focus more on on getting getting better, getting stronger, faster and and really getting mentally prepared to as well. Yeah, I think there was some peace of mind with that. I didn't know it was any later. I think just we we we looked at the schedule and mapped it out and at the end of the day I'm I'm excited to be back and go practice again and and not have to sit and watch. I think a lot of what we preach on the defensive side is the ball's our oxygen and you need oxygen to breathe. So, every play obviously you have your assignment, your alignment, your technique but at the end of the day you got to be thinking about the ball and going and getting the ball and that that stems from that mindset is all those turnovers. Yeah, I mean yeah, that's the I mean we you can see that it's on guys' minds. I mean, that's what happens when you preach that type of mindset is is it gets drilled in and when when guys are out there, it doesn't matter. Maybe you miss your assignment and all this, but at the end of the day, at the end of the play, all you got to be thinking about is the ball. So, getting to the ball, running there, punching out, getting getting tips, getting overthrows, everything like that. >> How would you say the personality of the defense has changed with Gerald McCoy and like >> I think both those guys have come in and really made an impact. I think vocally they're two guys that we can lean on. Quincy obviously having all the experience. We made fun of him today cuz he turned 30 yesterday. Uh Uh so, just his experience is is huge and then same with Gerald having a guy who can come in and and obviously lead by example, but also be able to you know, get us going too as well as is big and you know, their impact on the field is huge. >> Carson, what can you do to improve on your rookie of the years? >> A lot. Uh there's I mean, every aspect of the game you want to talk about. Getting better at stopping the run, getting better at uh seeing the formations before the ball snapped, better at dropping in coverage, rushing the passer. I think, you know, every area of my game has room to improve and that's what I'm trying to do this year. >> Okay, Carson, with without Miles here, obviously that's a big change, right? Um how do you think offenses are going to approach you schematically differently? It felt like last year things were kind of tilted away from him. Do you think it'll be more balanced this year? >> Uh I mean, you could see some. I think with our front uh you get attacked very similarly just because of how our our front four play. Um so, obviously you might see some changes or or more runs go to both sides and things like that, but um you know, at the end of the day we we put our 11 out there and and our whole goal is to to cause chaos on on the offensive side of the ball and make plays. >> Since you observe everything out there while watching What do you think of the the offense this year? What's the biggest difference that you're practicing against? >> I think, um, I mean, totally new offense to go against for us. I mean, we went went against it twice when we played, uh, Baltimore last year, but just able to see that that really everything's available. I think, um, there's, uh, a lot that they can do. I think we have, you know, the the receiver position has gained a lot of, uh, dynamic players, um, which defensively is is something that you always have to account for. And, um, same thing on the O-line. Um, and so I'm I'm ready, you know, as as a defense we go get the ball back to the offense and they're going to put some points on the board. >> You mentioned Easton before. Um, how have you seen him kind of develop? It looked like last year he was a guy that, you know, whatever, undrafted guy. And now this year he took takes your spot. He's calling the signals all the same. >> Yeah, I think just just the confidence he has when he steps on the field has been huge. It's not It's not easy to go out there and call the plays and and and run the show defensively. Um, and so him being able to go out there and really there's not there wasn't a step loss. I mean, the the control of the defense and and being able to get all the calls and everything like that. And then, um, just to the the effort to the ball. I mean, you can really see it with him. You saw it on on on the interception uh, two days ago. Um, at the end of the day to him the ball's oxygen. >> How have you guys responded taken to Mike Ruderford? I know how much you guys wanted to keep Jim Schwartz, but how has he >> I love, uh, having Rudy here. I think I've already learned a lot from him. I'm excited to to get into the year now. And, um, I was excited to practice all camp. So now I'm excited to practice today, um, and really get that going and and get our connection on the field going as well, you know, just as we have off the field. >> Whenever I asked coach Munchak about you, he kept saying, "We're really cautious. We're really cautious." If we were, you know, the regular season, how much time >> Uh, I mean, you could I might have a different answer than the trainers. I I could tell you that I could have a broken leg and I'd still play. So, that's what I'd say. >> When you talk about Uh I mean, it's it's really everything. um football is one of the the few sports where you can't practice as much as you'd like. We have 16 games and even in practice you can never go live and everything. And so, really there's an edge you can gain to to being able to go out there and watch film and and take everything in from that. Some of it and it's just watching a lot of stuff like that. And um you know, formation a lot of pre-snap stuff, all motions, how they come out the huddle, things like that. And and really you can just through watching it a lot you can pick things up. >> Thanks, Kirk. >> Yeah, thank you. >> Thanks, man. Last question.

title: Texans roster deadline: Who's making the team?! Who's cut? Who's not healthy?
text: Hi guys, Aaron Wilson back from Charlotte, North Carolina and the preseason is officially in the books. So now it's roster cut time and the Texans have already begun in earnest pairing down to the NFL roster limit of 53 players. They have until Sunday at 5:00 p.m. They've already begun. So let's start with the news. And a lot of this probably will not surprise you and some of this I've reported. Let me give it some context. So they released third quarterback Brett Ripen. Brett wasn't playing all that well. Had an interception in the preseason finale against the Panthers, but did throw one touchdown pass to Z Jones. I think there are other third quarterbacks potentially that could be on the practice squad or if you want to, I'm sure you could get him on your practice squad. There really isn't a, you know, a lot of urgency about the third quarterback. You guys get that. one of the tougher developments to come out of the game. Initially, they thought that Solomon Bird's ankle wasn't going to be that bad because of the way he was walking. He wasn't in a boot. Turns out it's a high ankle sprain per sources. And he's out 8 weeks. And what that means is this is just regular injury reserve, not designated for return specifically. So, they already have two guys that they're going to put on the IR designated for return. One of them we expected to be Tank Dell. But let's talk about Solomon for a moment. Solomon had made a strong bid to make the roster. He was doing a good job. He played very well in spurts, especially against the Chargers, but I thought that he showed some toughness against the Panthers and played a pretty good football game. All right, so he's out of the equation. And this is a very thin position because behind, you know, Will Anderson, Daniel Hunter, Javian Clowney still not 100%. And I heard the ankle is getting better. So, he should be back soon. But Dominic Robinson's still got a calf injury. So, who's the fourth defensive end? I think it's going to have to be somebody from outside the building if they don't think Robinson can do it. Robinson has got this calf injury that's lingered. It's been here for a while and he's missed a lot of practice time. So, at some point, you need to get him back out there. Ultimately, this may wind up falling to Logan Hall who has the versatility to play inside or outside. He's not a starter. So maybe he's the fourth in. He's doing a lot of double duty, but he's got to stay healthy. He's missing time right now. Also with an undisclosed lingering injury at the spring. He had knee tendonitis and he also had um if I remember correctly, a groin injury. Yeah, that's what it was. So you've got Mario Edwards Jr., but he's a defensive tackle. Naquon Jones got hurt. Not sure how bad it is, but he's injured. And as you know, they're going to move on from some good players like Sebastian Harsh had a great preseason finale and you definitely want him for the practice squad. He's a lock for that. But you're going to have to move on from Derek Parish, Dominic Bailey, Keonte Hamilton, and Ellie Gay, of course, is out for the season as I reported exclusively. Major knee injury, and they'd already lost Dylan Horton for the year to a torn Achilles, also one of my reports. So, I'll go down some of the roster cuts. And Caleb Johnson, the first Houston Christian player to make it to the NFL. When he was there, it was Houston Baptist. So, he was released. And Steven Hall, undrafted corner from Missouri, he's being released. They haven't officially processed release. They've just informed the players that they're going to be cut. And then, excuse me, they're also on the offensive side of the football. both of the running backs that they signed just a week ago. Duce Vaughn, former Dallas Cowboys running back. Yes. 5'5, 185 pounds. He's been released or is being released. And then also Owen Wright. And Owen actually played pretty well in the preseason finale despite a lack of blocking. So those are some of the moves that are pending. And then we expect a bunch more. We're hearing Z Jones is not going to make the team. I'm not completely surprised by that. Still no word on Sterling Shepard. A lot of these releases, these pending moves will be communicated on Sunday. Then word will filter out. So that's some of where it stands. And we'll go over the 53man roster here and talk about next steps. This might be bigger than some of the things that happened today, but I want to tell you about it. It's actually good news. Third running back Jawar Jordan is being cleared to practice medically and they will obviously, you know, take a little time to get him back up to full speed. But that's good news. He's finally back from that strained hip flexor. And what that means is Noah Whittington, who has a mild ankle injury, would be released and then head to the practice squad if he clears waiverss, which I believe that he would. So those are some of the developments there with third quarterback, defensive end, running back. They also released or are releasing two tight ends at the bottom of the depth chart and that's Lane Prior and Lewis Hansen. I thought Hansen did a good job. I'm hearing Hansen's not going to be on the practice squad. So, I'm not sure what they're doing with the that position. Brevin Jordan, they still haven't made a determination on him. I think it's going to be in reserve. Don't know if he'll be designated for return. This knee has been pretty chronic. So, that's what you've got. To me, a better candidate would be Braden Smith because I think he's going to need more time. Not saying like more than the four weeks, but there are some scenarios where they had to do that. Or they could carry him into the season slightly unhealthy and hope that he's back by say week two. Meanwhile, Trent Brown is going to hold it down at the right tackle job. And I think he'll be the starter as long as he's healthy. That he'll be ahead of Braden. Maybe at some point that changes, but right now that is the direction. That's the offensive line and that's where this thing is going. So, looking at a few other situations, just kind of knowing the team, let's tell you about it. So, the first four receivers are Nico Collins, Keshan Booty, and Jaylen Null, and Xavier Hutchinson. So, who's getting the last couple spots? Who's five and who's six? Do you keep Sterling Shepard as an experienced backup slot? I think you go with Lewis Bond and that's your fifth receiver. And then your six receiver, I would go between Jared Wayne and Justin Watson. I think Wayne can play special teams. Watson's a proven guy on special teams. We'll see. This is one of those Frank Ross picks, I believe. Offensive line. So, we know it's Aranter, left tackle, left guard Keelin Rage, centers Evan Brown, right guard Edingham, right tackle Trent Brown. Guys that didn't dress that are going to be on the team. That includes Wyatt Teller. And of course, you got Fabi Wayu. He did dress. He played. He played well. Could be your center of the future. Mark my words. All right. So, Jake Andrews, I don't think this bodess well for him. I think there's also scenarios where they don't keep Jake Andrews or Jared Patterson. That could happen. So, we'll see where this goes. Just can't see Tank Dell because he's not ready. They're not going to give him a spot at this time. So, those are a couple things going on there. And then other guys I you know obviously with the tight ends they're all set there. None of those guys played in the game. Dalton Schultz, Foster Maro, Marlon Klein, Cade Stove, and offensive line. Um, other ones I expect to release, uh, James Neil III, Sam Hagen, who didn't play well in the game, Jared Patterson, possibly Eli Cox, definitely Jared Kingston, and then, you know, at wide receiver parting ways with Trayvon Saunders, Josh Kelly. I expect Z Jones and Justin Watson likely. And we'll see. Is there a spot for Sterling Shepard? I'm not sure that there is. So, it almost found kind of felt like Demo Ryan was saying goodbye to those guys. And then British Brooks is back. I interviewed British. I posted that interview as well too on the channel. British back from that broken hand. And he's uh eager to make up for lost time. Let's go to the defense. So, here's what we know. We know it's the guys, the starters, the top ranked defense, Will Anderson Jr., Sheldon Rankings, Tommy Toi, Denil Hunter, Aziz Alshshire, the Mike linebacker in Pro Bowl selection, Henry Toto, his running partner there at linebacker spot, the will linebacker, the chase guy. Then Dererick Stingley Jr. and Kamari Lacader, Kayn Bulock, Reed Blankenship, and Jaylen Petri, the hard-hitting nickel. Okay, I kind of like the idea of keeping Elijah Huzzy as a backup. I also like the idea of keeping George ODM as a backup instead of Kavon Merryweather to go with Kamari Ramsey who we expect back soon. Don't know his injury. I was just told multiple times. It is not serious. We'll see. MJ Stewart I think will be on the physical perform. So that's another spot along with EJ Speed. I think Truman Smith makes it. I know you guys don't want to hear that, but I think Trmon does make the squad. I think that's going to happen. And then when I look at linebacker, I think Jake Hansen will stick. I know Wade Wood will be back next week from the broken thumb. He had surgery on. He'll be playing in the cast. And I like the idea of them keeping Jake Hmel, Jake Hansen, and then Jamal Hill versus Aiden Fischer. So, we'll see where that goes. Uh they've already cut Caleb Johnson, so we'll see. Jamal Hill sort of as he said in the interview, and I'll play it again, left it all out there on the field. So, we'll see where this goes. And the defensive tackle is complicated by K Naquon Jones. We'll see how serious his injury is. Special teams, that's all set. Kicker Kaim Fairburn, punter Kai Krueger won the job. Austin Brinkman, the long snapper, return man. Jaylen Null, punts and kickoffs. And then you have backup punt returners like Truman Smith and kickoff returner Woody Marks. uh corner Colin Wright still not healthy from the groin injury. I think that's what saves Truman Smith's job. Bryce Hall expect to be released. Brandon Codington expect to be released. Already releasing Steven Hall doesn't look like Aiden Fischer is necessarily getting a spot. So that's what's going down. Then of course all the other ones I've mentioned about injuries and that's your team. So couple other tidbits. Um I have a CJ Stout update for you. status quo in the negotiation, meaning not imminent, not close, still expecting at this rate for him to go into the season without a new contract. I don't think that's a controversy. I think that's fine because they can do it after the season. Logic really dictates for him, for David Mulligett, and I think a little bit for the Texans. I know everybody knows about JT, but it's a lot of, you know, great receivers on our team. Speaking of Keen Keenan, that's another great addition. So, of course, we're going to be able to make points, you know, put points. So, >> we saw the entire bench clear when DJ Giddens got in the end zone for that touchdown.
