Yeah. I feel honestly looking back about the whole process, the earlier the easiest part was the earlier rehab and then the hardest parts been camp, you know, >> when you weren't kicking like you could pick. >> Yeah. You have really high expectations for yourself and I knew what I was capable of and not performing that way consistently and you know day after day during camp just grinds at you. Not to mention, you're in football for 12 hours a day. So, I don't get to do my normal things, which is hang out with family and friends outside of football and go to my Bible studies, which keeps me fulfilled. So, it just like wears on you day after day. And so, training camp is always about the battle of the mind, battling yourself every single day, day in and day out. I'm glad that I and I'm proud that I've gotten to the point where I feel like I've turned a corner and I've turned a page. But the crazy thing is, and I think this every year, thought it two years ago, I thought it last year, you work so hard. and you put so much effort in just to make it through can season haven't even started yet. Like none of these games like count, you know, and so that's the crazy part is you put so much effort in just earning a potential right to start off the season and start over again. >> This is kind of what I'm I'm used to it. Um, you know, I was playing with Antonio Gates and Antonio Gates was a lot of the TJ we watch in practice. So, um, now now it's me. So, I mean, you put put in longevity and have have enough years, you'll eventually become the TJ. As we wrap up preseason play, what areas do you think the team still needs to pick it up a little bit? >> I don't know. We we we haven't really, you know, played a real game. So, um I think just just everybody being healthy, everybody being ready, um you know, week one versus Baltimore and um coming in ready to go. >> Keen and I talked to Alex just earlier today about things. What are the things that you've observed with the rest of your life that you can mess with thus far? >> That's the knowledge of everybody. Everybody knows what they're doing. Everybody knows the playbook really well. Um and that that's half the battle. You can play fast. You don't have to think too much. And then um you know, obviously Reggie Wayne, he's the he's the receiver coach. So, everybody has those small techniques and um you know, little little things that they can you know, use to get open with, you know, just with his knowledge as well. >> How much fun is it just to be back with Shane again? >> Yeah, that's great. Um he's my guy. uh you know we we go back and um just used to used to the offense being ran this way being called this way and um used to the terminology too. >> Obviously kind of like your career what I guess you still chasing come back to >> I just love the game and um just about playing being in the locker room meeting meeting guys uh building relationships and um you know always goes back to the game that you love. >> I mean it's definitely great to you know make that play right before the season going right into the season. So, um I think that was great to, you know, end the drought real quick going into the year. So, um yeah, preseason or not, that's still a great play. Um you know, cuz they don't come that much that often. So, yeah. >> Good opportunity to celebrate with the guys too after it. >> For sure. Uh you know, the reality of it is some of the guys, you know, might not be here, you know, um that's just part of like the business. Um, so it's just good to be able to have those great moments with some of these guys that might not be here, might be on another team, you know, it's just was a blessing to go on this go on this ride and um go through training camp otaas and everything with these guys and you know to just be able to learn some stuff from them. They learned some stuff from me. So yeah, >> I know you guys are really frustrated with how you played against the Falcons. What do you think you showed today in terms of improvements? I know you had three picks for the defense, three turnovers for the defense, one for special teams. That's got to make you feel good, right? I mean, uh, those plays for sure, but, you know, um, we don't want to get any points up, you know what I'm saying? Especially touchdowns. So, there's still a lot to go back to the drawing board and talk about. Um, still a lot of tape to go over and um, yeah, but those three turnovers were were great. >> What specifically are you looking at in terms of areas that you got to clean up? >> I mean, just trying to see how we put how we allow uh, points, you know? So, those are the main things. Just trying to see how we allowed those points and trying to just clean that up. Where do you feel like this secondary is at now that we're kind of through the preseason here? >> Uh, I think we in a pretty good spot. Um, you know, I think when everybody is healthy, you know, top defensive defensive back group. Um, but yeah, just continuing to mess and gel and, you know, we ready to just go out there and just show what we can do. >> How would you assess your final preseason game performance out there today? >> Uh, you know, I thought the first drive went really well. Um, unfortunately got two drives. You know, I had the second quarter. Um I think estimating or you know usually around two or three drives every quarter. So just hoping to get one more in. Um but the first drive went well. Second drive um got to a check. Uh should have executed a little better. But um yeah, I thought it went okay. Uh you hang your head high on on on the first drive and you know I thought it went pretty smoothly. So um at least there's some positivity uh you know looking back at the game. most about. So, this is my friend, my guy, but also something that he wants to do. >> It's really good question. Um, you know, I think when you enter a quarterback competition, um, you just got to keep reminding yourself like, hey, you know, my best is good enough to win and Anony's best is good enough to win. Uh, you never want to win a competition because you maybe you both played bad and but you just didn't play as bad. um you know me and him are on the same page where it's like hey man I'm rooting for you um you know I know he's rooting for me uh you know who who can reach their full potential right who can play to their full potential and uh yeah um obviously somebody I really respect and love um you know if there's one guy who who you know I wake up in the morning and I go to the facility and I'm excited to you know see every day and joke around with is is Anthony. So, um it's been a really good and healthy competition. Um so, I guess we'll we'll find out, you know, kind of where we stand tomorrow. >> How will you handle these next 24 hours? Like, how are you going to mentally deal with that? >> I don't I don't know. Um well, I Yeah, I don't I don't know. If you got any good answers, let me know because uh you know, I haven't really been in this situation before. Um so, I'm open for suggestions. Blake said he's going to go fishing. Maybe >> Yeah, it's a great idea. It's a really good idea. Um that might go putt a little bit on the golf. I don't know. But um probably spend it with my wife. Uh obviously got married, you know, 5 months ago, so I'm kind of very excited to see her and you know, just she always just brings me down to earth. Um and uh it's like a sanctuary going home. So I'm very thankful for her. the pass on that that interception. Is that a ball you like in hindsight like to have back or did you feel like it was a good throw when you made it? >> Uh yeah, obviously yeah any pick you you want the throw back? Um not really disappointed in anything other than you know get getting everybody aligned um in the right position making sure um I'm making the right checks up front uh make sure I'm I'm not in that position again. But the throws, you know, you can look back at the throws. I'm not really worried about any any throws really. It's more just uh the decision-m and operation side of things. That's those are the things that as a quarterback you kind of look back and regret on. >> Riley, one thing that we talked about over the course of the preseason when you had the opportunity is you wanted to play without hesitation. How much do you feel like you were able to to do that? >> Yeah, I think today uh was definitely the the best um I've played in that context so far. I really felt comfortable out there. Um felt confident. Um, even on the interception, it's like, all right, you know, I it is what it is. You know, I I felt good. Felt felt like I was seeing it pretty well. So, um, yeah, every week has been, you know, a lot better for me mentally, whether, you know, I don't I don't know the stats or anything, whether it proves it or not, but mentally truly felt better every week going out there and, uh, felt very prepared coming into this game. >> Um, just the only injury we had, you guys saw Coleman Owen uh, concussion there. U, but I was pleased uh, overall. uh with the first offense, first defense the way they started. Um we got some good work in today with the other guys. Got to be better on a few areas, especially third down, both sides of the ball, but overall pleased with the work uh in the preseason that happened. >> What's your appreciation for Trager where he came from from the Vegas game where he blows his knee out where he is now? >> Yeah, I think there's a lot of appreciation coming off an ACL to be where he's at. Um to kick the 60 yarder today uh was huge. So um I'm really pleased with where he's at. You think you can get a draft pick or something? >> Yeah, I mean I'll defer to talking about trades and all that right now. >> Yeah. >> How would you evaluate your quarterback play in the first half? >> Yeah, I thought uh Anthony had some good drives for sure. I think you finished seven to 10. Uh made some good throws. Uh did some good things. I think Riley did some good things as well. Just obviously don't want to turn it over there in the red zone. Um, but I thought both of them did some good things >> for Keenan to just get in, get that catch and get out. What do you think that just did for him today? >> Yeah, it was good. You know, wanted to get him a touch there. Um, and obviously got a good coverage and he went on the route and, uh, Anthony delivered a good ball, so it was good to get him out there. >> Between now and the start of the regular season, what's your biggest concern for this team and how confident are you that you can correct it and give them the right track? >> Well, I think uh, I look at like, you know, everything. I take it all in account all the practices and stuff. I feel really good about our group in general to be completely honest. Um both sides of the football um with our starters out there. So I do feel good about that. I think it's complimentary football is the biggest thing uh going into a season. You know, we get a takeaway, we got to go do something with it, so on so forth. So I think the cop burning football thing is a big thing that we need to be great at this year. >> Shane, what are the the hardest conversations or the most complicated conversations these last 24 hours with? >> Yeah, I mean there's going to be some moving parts here tonight uh tomorrow morning. Um, obviously it's, you know, those spots. I mean, we know the spots that are locked up, but then there's going to be some conversations on, you know, the depth pieces and how they can help us, whether it's special teams and where we use them offensively, defensively, um, and just kind of finalizing those touches, you know, tonight and tomorrow morning. >> Most of the takeaways came from rookies today. What does that tell you? Like how pleased have you been with the rookie class? >> Yeah, I've been really pleased with those guys. Those vi those guys go violently after the football, and that's what you want on defense. guys attacking the football. Obviously getting the tackle first, but really going after the ball and to get the turnovers today is huge. It always gives you a chance to win um when we get that done. >> Celebration. >> It was. I wanted those guys to have fun. I want to say, "Hey, shoot. It's our last preseason. It's the last time this group's going to be together." Um and so go have fun with it. Uh bring energy and every time we score, go celebrate together. >> Similar to Shider Force Buckner kind of long road back. He's getting back out there. I know he's played a million games, big games, but getting back out there. It means a ton for the group. Um, I got so much respect for him and his career and what he's done so far up to this point. To come back from the neck injury, um, is phenomenal. You know, he puts in the work. Um, one of the best guys I've ever been around as far as locker room guy, player, teammate, um, leadership abilities. Um, he's as good as he gets. >> You let some of the other assistants call plays today? >> Yeah, we kind of been doing that all preseason. So, um, you know, we let some guys call a quarter. Like today, I called the first quarter with the starters. Tommy Manny called a quarter. Reggie called the third quarter. Um, and Tanny called the fourth and then the games before. Same thing on defense. Chris Hwitt, KO, um, all those guys, Betcher, everyone's been calling stuff. >> Why haven't you done that years past? >> Yeah. Yeah, I've been doing that. I think it's an opportunity for those guys to grow. You know what I mean? I think everyone has aspirations of being a coordinator and so it gives them that opportunity um, to go out there and call games.

title: Insiders: Colts vs. Lions preview, some starters will play
text: We are here for the Colts third and final preseason game leading into the start of the 2026 regular season. A lot to watch today. Um, Joel >> Is there? Are you sure? >> Well, we get a chance >> [laughter] >> the the biggest thing is we get a chance to see some starting caliber players on the field for the first time. The Colts have played as you would expect with second and third string guys throughout these first two preseason games. We will get to see some, not all of the starters on offense and defense give us a run through on what uh head coach Shane Steichen said that we should expect to see today. >> Yeah, it's going to be eight to 12 snaps for the starters. Uh I think he said he DeForest Buckner can take himself out whenever he wants. >> Yeah, one or two snaps is I think the way he put it. >> So, eight to 12 snaps is essentially if they go down and score on the first drive, they'll be done. [music] If they punt, they're probably going to come back out for another one. Uh you're not going to see a lot of the skill players though. Daniel Jones not playing, Jonathan Taylor's not playing. I wouldn't expect to see Tyler Warren, I wouldn't expect to see Alec Peters, or Josh Downs. I'm kind of surprised that Keenan Allen is going to play, but for the most part you're not going to see those guys because they're dealing with either nagging injuries or coming off of an injury and they don't want to risk them. It's a little surprising to me they're playing as many starters as they are. >> Yeah, we'll see a little bit more depth or a little bit more um from a numbers perspective on the defensive side of the ball. Um JuJu Smith-Schuster will not be out there. He told us himself earlier this week that he will not he's still working himself back from a back injury. Um something that we have written about he's going to have to deal with throughout this season. Um by the time we get through the first drive, first couple drives, um get to see get a chance to see what the offense look like. What will you be watching out for the most for the rest of this game today? >> Does does one of these backup quarterbacks make a real case for themselves? You know, Anthony Richardson came the closest in the first preseason game, but from what my my understanding is it's really still neck and neck to the point that might not name a number two quarterback until further close to the regular season opener. And really the only reason they have to do that is because they have to designate which quarterback is going to be the third one for emergency purposes. Um I'm curious to see can Anthony Richardson, can Riley Leonard, can somebody make an impression in this game that puts them over the top? >> Yeah, Anthony Richardson will get a chance to start this game. As Joel mentioned, not a whole lot of skill position players outside of Kylen Allen that he will get to play with. He will play the entire first quarter. >> [music] >> Riley Leonard will then sub in for the entire second quarter with the second string and then Easton Stick, their fourth string quarterback throughout the preseason, will get a chance to play the entire second half with whoever else is filling coming off the bench. Some other stories and then we will of course be providing you live updates throughout the day tomorrow when the Colts starts narrowing down their roster from 90 men to 53 and then we'll have some more stories on that as well. Keep checking in on indystar.com as well as our IndyStar Colts YouTube channel and we'll check in with you guys later today.

title: Coach Jeff Hafley meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: just to start. Um, obviously we all know what today and tomorrow are, so those are pretty tough days and we're going through the process right now and I'm sure there's a lot of questions on cuts and everything that is going to happen. Um, I will respectfully defer those to Sully who will be speaking to you um, I think within the next few days. Um, I think that's important that um, [clears throat] you know, we we let him handle those questions. But anything else regarding the players in the game? I'll be happy to answer as always. >> We'll start with Barry. >> What's up, Barry? >> All right, Jeff. [clears throat] So, this is not uh a cuts question at all. It is a bit of a roster question. Obviously, teams have beginning a couple years ago those two extra roster spots to play with by putting two players on IR concurrently with cuts tomorrow. Uh Trey Moore would seem logical for one. Is Kenneth Grant's injury such that you think he's a logical option for the others? Just let him heal for four weeks and then bring him back. >> Yeah, I mean those are discussions that we're having and I think that will clear up within the next few days here as we get closer getting down to 53 and then talking about who we can who we feel good about, you know, truthfully getting ready for the first game. Um, so those are questions as we make these decisions today, tomorrow, and then talk to Kyle and and have a good plan. But Barry, there certainly that is one that we've had the conversation about. >> Thanks. And one last quick thing, Will Casmic, can you tell us how serious his issue is? >> Yeah, he'll be week to week. Um, he [clears throat] will be out this week. Thank you, >> Joe Shad. >> Hey, Jeeoff. Good morning. Um, at the moment. Do you believe the team is likely to keep two quarterbacks? >> I do. >> Okay. And at the moment, do you think the team is likely to keep four tailbacks? >> Um, that's a good question. I I think that's you know I think those are still some of the discussions going on and I think that will clear up between today and tomorrow. >> Thanks Jeff. >> You're welcome. Sorry can't give you much better than that. >> Okay >> Chris. >> Hey Jeff. Um I got a question about the starters and how much playing time they got in the preseason. By my calculation they got two joint practices in one quarter. And you know, I don't think that that's really too far out of line with the rest of the NFL. But my question to you is, uh, two questions. Number one, what was your preeason plan as far as the starters and did injuries alter that, especially in game three? And number two, your approach and the the amount of time the starters have gotten. Do you think it puts you at a disadvantage in say weeks one and two of the regular season? Um, to your first question, you know, I I thought I alluded to this in, you know, my thought going in, you know, very detailed plan. You know, I said it last night, in a perfect world, I I would have loved to have seen the starters play 20 25 plays maybe into the second quarter and see how the game goes. Um, but that just wasn't best for for where we're at right now as a team. That's not best for the Dolphins. it's not best for trying to get guys ready to go play in that first game. Um those are the decisions that we have to make. So whether or not that's going to limit certain guys um that's going to prepare our team to be most ready to play week one and I strongly believe that. Um and I know everyone in the organization does as well. And and and as far as the the rest of the league, do you think that what what the amount of time that your starters got, I mean, it seems like in the 17 game schedule, that's kind of the way it goes in preseason. Is that a correct read on the situation? >> I mean, I think every team's different. There's some teams that did one joint practice, like the Falcons had one joint practice, so they played their starters yesterday for however many plays. We had two joint practices where we were, you know, a lot of our ones got 40 or close to 40 plus reps in real football, which is probably more than you would play your starters in a preseason game. I mean, we're not going to get those guys out there for 80 plays. Um, you know, we feel like the work that they got, um, will be sufficient enough with these next two weeks to get them ready to play. Um, you know, but there's a fine line like like I talked about, Chris, you we got to make sure that that the guys who we deem as starters are going to be healthy enough to play um in Vegas and that's more important than a preseason game. >> Gotcha. Thanks, >> Travis. >> Hey, coach. Good morning, or I guess good afternoon here. Uh, I've always enjoyed to hear you talk about your plans and kind of the evolving nature of what you, you know, portray for the next week or month or so. So, I wanted to ask you what the next two weeks look like in terms of conditioning, game planning. How do you want to attack the 14 days that you have before Vegas? >> Yeah, we'll take um we'll have really three and a half good practices this week. We'll loosen them up a little bit Monday. Get some individual work in guys who haven't done a lot. We'll have the practice squad guys hopefully by later in the afternoon on Monday and then we'll kind of go through a Wednesday, Thursday, Friday kind of uh rehearsal of what a inseason three days will look like. Um coaches will start game planning. We'll start introducing some of the Raiders scheme this week and start doing some scout work and some carded work. But I think this week is still really important for us to go good on good to continue to get ready um to play because I think as much as you can go speed on speed, I do think that's very important. Um I also we got to make sure we're careful because we have a bunch of guys right now that are still not ready to practice. So we got to do some jog through periods where they'll be able to go and and continue to get work because we got to make sure we're healthy going into the first game. So again, there's there's a fine line between I want to go full speed ahead and and do all the things that I love to do, but at the same time, I got to make sure that we're healthy. >> Very good. Thank you, >> Kyle. >> Hey, good afternoon, coach. >> Hey, Kyle. um in listening to you over the last month talk about how you guys have gone about camp and preeason, feeling that conviction that you have about staying basic and focusing on player evaluation instead of winning calls. I'm just kind of curious what your influences are that have led to that conviction in you. Is that Jeff Hafley, the program builder at BC? Is that coaching influences that you've had from coaches you've worked under? Just kind of curious where all that conviction comes from about why this was right for your team. >> Well, I think it's a collaboration of our whole entire staff and our organization and where we are as a team. I mean, we're young and we have a lot of guys who are, you know, don't have a lot of experience in the NFL. title: Todd Bowles: Who’s Making Their Case For The Roster | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: First question will come from Greg Auman. >> Hey Todd, I hope you're doing well getting back home. I just wanted to ask you first about Mo Kamara. Just wanted to know if you knew more about that knee injury from last night. >> Uh he's going to get an MRI this afternoon. He should be fine. >> Okay. He showed up definitely. He made a play on teams as well. Pyburn I think is leading the league in sacks in preseason, so he's made a great case for himself at a deep position, so it's something we definitely have to look at. And the other one was What was the other one you gave me? >> Wisdom, Fordham. >> Fordham. Fordham's been consistent throughout. He's a tough gritty player. He's very smart and he's very aware and he seemed to be at the right place all the time. >> With respect to Pyburn, obviously he's one of those guys that has the opportunity to go back college. Have you talked to him about whether he would do that if in fact he didn't make the regular roster and you would want to put him on the practice squad or something? >> We haven't talked to him I haven't talked to him about that. We have talked about the situation. He didn't know what he was going to do at the time or how he felt. He has some people that he's talking to and that was again that was probably about a week ago, so I don't know where his mindset is when in that regard, but it's something we have to sort through. >> Thanks, coach. >> Scott Reynolds. >> Morning, Todd. Obviously, it's preseason and your offense has started to play about eight snaps or so and Zach Robinson isn't showing much of his playbook at all, but when you face his offense in practice, what excites you about Zach's scheme and maybe gives your defense some issues generally speaking? >> I think he's very good at tweaking things within the system, making it look the same. Obviously, game plan-wise, I think he's he's very good at understanding what you guys have what strength and know how to get them open and know how to run the football that way and try to get the extra half man. So, that that's what I'm looking forward to. >> And then when it comes to the receiver position, it's it's deep and it's talented, but are you concerned over the overall health of the wide receiver position? That's a a position that's suffered a great deal of injuries over the last two seasons and even in training camp this year, does that maybe prompt you to keep more receivers just because of that? >> Uh it's it's been a question that we got to answer. Um it's one of them, but we expect J Mac and hopefully Mekhi to come back before week one and have be at full strength that way. So, that'll have a lot to do with whether we keep the extra one or not and how healthy these guys are going forward. >> Greg Auman. >> Todd, I know you addressed this a little bit last night, but just just want to ask you the overall offensive performance to have less than 100 yards. I know you're just trying to get through the game. Is that the easiest explanation or or is it concerning that they weren't able to move the ball more consistently? >> No, that was concerning. It's not an easy explanation at all. You got to get more than 100 yards and you don't want to get shut out ever, regardless of who's playing in preseason. We're trying to win the game. We're trying to be physical up front on both sides of the football. Defensively, the guys up front played well. Offensively, they didn't. >> Todd, as as you're trying to make the the tough final decisions for the 53, does does having injured reserve to start the season like with the intent to return, does that help you at all? Are there guys that are in play for that or is that not really the case right now? >> We'll get the injury report today, but there are a few guys that might be in place for that. We don't have as many as we thought we would have, but there's probably one or two guys in place for that. >> Rich Cimini. I think I know where this is going, but coach, have you decided uh whether whether you can keep three quarterbacks on the 53-man roster and if that's your plan? >> It's something we got to talk about uh probably right after this. We're going to meet on it this morning and we're going to go over some things that way. It's a discussion, but it's not a definite. >> And and uh what's what's the pros and cons? I mean, obviously the pros is you keep an extra quarterback, but but how difficult is it in this day and age to have that many on the active roster? >> It's difficult because you you probably need the spot for somewhere else as far as teams or an extra rusher or an extra back or an extra offensive lineman. So, knowing that guy's not going to play in case of emergency, I think every position would like to have insurance behind the insurance and that's something you got to weigh the pros and cons of and, you know, kind of make that decision going forward. >> Coach, I understand that some of the guys that were on special teams last night are ultimately going to be cut um when the roster cuts come down, but it how have you evaluated Danny Smith's performance? I know that sometimes you know, you want change to happen instantly and everything to get better, but have you seen enough progress on special teams that the punt return for a touchdown notwithstanding, but do you feel like special teams is is moving in a certain direction and and uh and what direction is that? >> I feel like it's moving in a positive direction. I think Danny's been great and he's been great for the room. You know, we're trying to kick off and punt because we're trying to see who can make the team. We haven't put our total unit out there together yet. We've put guys out there that were battling for positions against each other, try to make them compete and make the team that way. But from an overall special teams standpoint, Danny's done an excellent job and we put the guys out there that need to be out there and in the right places, we'll be fine. >> And then after you had a chance to look at the film, what did you think about Benjamin Morrison's preseason debut last night on special teams and on defense? >> Biggest thing he was healthy and he was in shape. Obviously, he needs time on task at the position to get some of the rust off of that way, but he he played fast and he played hard on teams and you know, he didn't have much action his way. He did get a tackle in there on a cutback run, but other than that, it's just a matter of him just getting reps and seeing everything. So, the health part was the biggest thing and he played a whole half, so that was good to see. >> Greg Auman, if any media have questions, please raise your hand. >> Coach, what you were talking about special teams, one job we really haven't talked about at all is long snapper. You guys have Evan Deckers back from last year. I think he was the first guy in in all three games, but you did alternate him and Daily last night. Just curious about that job and and with the that's still a competition. >> It was still a competition going into last night. Again, we'll evaluate that as we meet with Danny when he comes in and we'll kind of go from there. >> Okay, thanks. >> Here you go. >> Um are you in a position where you can keep four running backs and and I know you're still working on the puzzle in in of having all the pieces together where you keep three quarterbacks or not, but can you maybe shed some light on how the battle for the third string running back between Josh Williams and Sean Tucker has gone this preseason, whether it's kickoff returns or whether it's as a runner or a receiver and pass protector? >> That was a tough battle. It kind of went back and forth every game. Uh both of them can run the ball, both of them return kicks, obviously. Uh both of them try to tackle on kickoff and punt team, and it's a matter of keeping four running backs, uh three quarterbacks, you know, there's an extra receiver involved, obviously a corner involved, a defensive lineman. So, all that's going to be in the discussion, but that'll be a tough call because they're both good football players. >> Thanks, Todd. >> Last one from Rick Stroud. >> I'm sure I think most people recognize your offensive line when it's healthy is one of the tops in the NFL. Um how do you feel about your depth, though? I know you played a lot of guys last night, but um just the inconsistency there uh to run the football, really even protect, you know, either quarterback. >> Well, with Chuke out and with Schooler out, you know, from a tackle standpoint, the depth is thin with with three tackles out and Tristan and Luke not playing, really four tackles out. Uh inside, you got to worry about the guard. Feeney's experienced, and he can play both spots, but the other guys got to come on a little more. Haggard and uh Klein has really got to come on a little bit more, and it was one guy here or there last night that kind of butchered the whole thing, and they just didn't play well, but overall depth, when you're keeping eight or nine, we think we got decent eight depth from that standpoint, but we can't get anybody hurt. >> Got you. Thanks, coach. >> All right, that's all we have. Thanks, coach. >> Thanks.

title: Makai Lemon & More on Their Preseason Game VS the Bengals
text: First preseason game for you, just how did it go out there for you tonight? >> Yeah, I was just excited to get out there, you know, with the guys before the actual real season get out there. So, you know, felt good though. >> You're catching passes from Tanner, from Andy. Can you describe the differences between the two? >> Shoot. Nah, not really. You know, that ain't my focus or anything like that. You know, I'm just making sure that I do my job and then my job on it. >> What are the things you take away from this to learn from? >> Shoot. Everything, really. Route running, obviously catching the ball. Just little things like that. >> What about the the pass that went off your hands? Was that a timing thing? Like you take us through that play there or >> It's a drop. It hit my hands. It went through my hands. I got to catch them. You know, learn from it. Um you know. Yeah. >> You've been working out with Jaylen in the your week back and after practice and all that. Just time spent with Tanner maybe helps you out? What do you attribute that to? >> Nah, I don't think it's that. Just making sure I catch the rock when every time it comes. No matter where it's at. You know, that's on me. >> What about the play that you and Elijah collided in on the route? What happened there? >> Shoot, we just collided, really. You know, that's all it is. >> How so? >> We just collided. Yeah. >> How did you What happened on the punt return? You know, I guess it was the first chance you had, correct, uh to do that. Have you done much in practice and what did you think about how it turned out today? >> Yeah, for sure. I feel like, you know, punts ain't going always be, you know, right to you. So, I just might got to make sure, you know, I stay on my toes, stay ready. Um you know, for things like that happening in the game. So, you know, when they do come about, you know, I'm ready. >> Is returning something you enjoy? >> Yeah, for sure. You know, coaches trust me enough to, you know, be out there. So, I got to make sure that, you know, I know to do my job, you know, to the fullest. Um wherever the ball's going to be at. So, yeah. >> What did you think about the speed of the game? First time actually live action. >> Um it it was cool. Like, you know, practicing with the guys, you know, that I've been scrimmage, it's it's like the same thing. >> It didn't it didn't seem any faster than than the practices. >> Nah. >> What's the benefit for you to to get this game out of the way before the regular season? >> Um just cleaning up little mistakes really. Um you know, dropping the ball like that, you know, glad it happened in the preseason, so you know, come around, you know, September, you know, things like that won't happen. >> How prepared do you feel for that opener a couple of weeks away? >> Yeah, I feel real prepared, but you know, we still got some time, so you know, I got to make sure, you know, I lock in. Each week, so >> You worked hard to come back from the you worked hard to come back from the hamstring. What are the challenges in only playing one preseason game? >> Um but I ain't no really no challenges really, you know, getting a bunch of reps, you know, in practice, and then obviously out here, but you know, when the game come about, man, it's it's ready to go. >> You had a few practices now and then playing in a game. How does the hamstring feel? >> Yeah, it seems to feel great. Ain't no problem. >> Micah, what were the guys telling you on the sidelines when you would come off the field? >> Yeah, you learn from it, then forget about it, you know, you can't beat yourself about it, and then next next play mentality really, so I just appreciate the guys, you know, having my back, you know, I'm real hard on myself, you know, I'm a perfectionist, so um when things like that do come about, you know, I just got to forget about it, and yeah, move on. >> Is that something that's difficult for you to just kind of forget a a bad play and move on sometimes? >> Um I feel like it's definitely tough, but you know, when you're a professional like this, you know, you got to do those type of things, just forget about it, you know, so Um that's all it is. >> Do you feel it's almost good Do you feel it's almost good to get some of these things out of the way now before the games start counting in a couple of weeks? >> Yeah, definitely. Like I said, I'm glad it happened, you know, during the preseason game, so you know, come around September, you know, it's it's it's the real deal. >> Obviously, you you missed some time obviously with with the injury. How would you summarize your first NFL NFL training camp? a blessing, really, you know? Just blessed to be out here, be where my feet are at, you know, with this team, um with the guys. So, um I couldn't, you know, ask to be, you know, anywhere else. Just blessed. >> We'll do a couple more. >> Thank you, Micah. >> Thank you, Micah. Thank you, Micah. Appreciate it. >> How did the you know, first half that you had tonight How did it feel out there? >> Yeah. Um obviously um had some frustrations, had had had some balls that, you know, I wish I could have back. Um obviously specifically the one to Kobi. Um I just got to hit that or um just being on the same page as with some guys. Um >> That was a That was a tough one. >> Um yeah, just you know, wish we would have executed a little better. And that's specifically me. >> What are your takeaways >> I mean, it was a good game. What's your comfort comfort level with this? >> Yeah, I think it grows every day. Um just obviously in the game, but also in practice and just getting reps on different plays. Um I feel like the offense is always evolving um to kind of what we do to our guys, and we're kind of learning um who who runs which routes and who does these things, and so I think there is a little bit of a growing process of, you know, let's let's see what this guy can do, and let's see how um we react. Um but I think each day, you know, we're we're sharpening the the the knife, I guess. Um and we're getting better and better each day. >> What happened on the on the interception on the pass to Micah? >> Um yeah. Um I got to get the ball down. Uh I know it's not fun as a receiver to, you know, put your hands over your head when um you're going across the middle. Um and so as as a quarterback, I I got to get the ball down to make that make that easier catch for him. >> What do you think it was today that didn't really allow you to get into a rhythm? I'd say that we just, you know, didn't feel like we found a great rhythm. Um and uh yeah, that's it. >> Overall, how would you Overall, how would you assess your preseason and your >> Yeah, I I I thought it was good. I felt like I felt like I definitely got better throughout um throughout training camp. Felt a lot more comfortable um just with the offense, calling the plays, um you know, getting guys in the right spots. I feel like at the beginning you're you're thinking a ton, trying to, you know, just what is what is my job? And then by the end of training camp you can get guys on the right page and they have questions about their routes to them or their depth or whatever it is. And as a quarterback you got to have all the answers. And so um just learning that way um feel like we've made, you know, a huge step and we're going to continue to um grow in that way. >> How do you feel like you mentally handled, you know, this year versus last going knowing that there was no competition for the backup job a year ago this year obviously >> Yeah. >> uncertainty you got to love to compete. Um and and if you don't then you're not really going to survive in this league. Um Andy and I like I I I think everyone realized we have a really good relationship. Um but at the same time when we're on the field like we we like to compete against each other and we we want the best for each other and you know, we're cheering each other on. I hope, you know, people realize that and get to see that. We're we're genuinely happy for each other when the other one's playing well. Um but, you know, we we want to do our best as well and and you got to love to compete and that's that's part of the business. That's, you know, we've both been talking about it, you know, there can only be one, no QB2 and um we're both going to try to make our cases for it. >> What would you say your confidence level is at given, you know, learning a new scheme, having in a competition really for the first time? >> Mhm. Yeah, I would say um kind of what I was saying before, just growing every day. Um being in competitions been great. Uh I feel like every year you're either you're competing with somebody, you're competing for your spot, you're competing to prove that you belong, you know, especially me as a sixth round draft pick, you know, the first year that I came in I was I was not um automatically going to make the team and, you know, going to whatever it is. And so um each year you're trying to prove yourself um whether that's competing with yourself, competing um against other guys, whatever it is. Um and so each year you just, like we said, you got to love to compete. >> How did you think McCaffrey did? You guys haven't really been practicing much together cuz you're running with the the ones, but how did you think he did and and you know, what happened I guess on that one downfield attempt? >> Uh my what what >> Second pass to him, he kind of did a he was a little bit of an out got he got undercut. >> Oh, yeah. Um we'll see the film. I don't I I don't know. Um I I it's hard to answer. I'm I apologize. We'll see the film. Um Um ultimately the the DB got his hand on it, so I I got to put the ball outside a little bit more um and let it be us or nobody. but yeah, it's hard to say without seeing film. >> What's the communication with the coaches been like in terms of setting expectations for what this this was and what they were looking for? >> Yeah, um I I think they've they've been open about what they want to see us grow in of of learning the new offense, taking command, um moving the ball, um and so that's that's been great. Um and ultimately they want us to compete, you know, I I I think that that that's part of it of putting us in situations in practice or whatever it is in the game, not telling us how many plays we're going to get, not telling us when we're going to go in, um and then all of a sudden like as a backup quarterback usually is in the regular season just at a second's notice you got to go in and perform. Um and so I think they've done a really good job preparing us that way of, you know, this is this is going to be your job in the season of at a moment's notice being able to go into the play go in two play and uh and perform. >> Take two more pretenders. >> What's next in terms of did they relay like when when the decision's going to come down and all that sort of >> Uh they haven't given us a time frame. so yeah, we'll we'll see. Obviously watch the film, continue to uh continue to get better and yeah, we'll see. >> Based on your performance this summer, how do you feel like your chances are? >> Um I feel good. I I I feel confident um in my ability to to run the offense, to play the offense. and so we'll we'll we'll see what happens. I'm excited. >> Andrew, I asked click for you from the jump tonight. Can you talk about that a little bit? >> Yeah, I felt comfortable out there. You I think uh uh just you know, kind of getting into a rhythm and getting some quick completions early and then we were able to uh hit a couple explosives out there. So, I think that was the biggest thing is just you know, felt comfortable, felt in rhythm and you know, we moved the ball offense. >> Andy, I ask with no indication or knowing what's ahead, but like just as one possible option, is this a is this a place you would stay on the practice squad? Or what? If that was it on the line. >> I mean, we'll see. There's a lot that's going to be going on. So, um we're just going to let it all play out. >> I'm sorry if you've already been asked this. What kind of case do you think you made this preseason to be on the 53? >> Yeah, I think I think I feel comfortable in the offense. I think there's value um that I can bring with just the experience that I've had, the you know, the things that I'm able to do in the meeting room and just the things that I understand about just you know, playing the this position. So, I I feel like that there's some value there and yeah, you know, I I feel really good about where I'm at. >> What's the dynamic been like between yourself and and Tanner? Both going you know, both competing, but you know, obviously having similar goals. >> Yeah, you know, it's uh it's fun to talk about Tanner when he's sitting right there, you know? but Tanner and I have been we've been great. You know, it's been fun from the beginning. I think uh that's one thing every we're rooting for each other. We want everybody to do uh really well and uh I'm I'm Tanner's biggest fan and I felt the same out there for uh for me, you know? I rooted for him every time that he he was going and he was doing the same. >> You made it through your your first preseason, these three games. What do you think you learned most? >> I learned many things from like especially the coaching point and playing the game for the first time. I learned many things from coach Kingsbury and the rest of the veterans. Like uh my power level and what to what to what to see when when playing the game, yeah. And it's amazing to learn the game and at the same time play the game, right. >> When you think about how far you've come over the last month or so, what are you most happy about? >> I'm most happy about the confidence that I have during game because like two three months ago I was not this confident and when he when coach Klint told me that it's going to be tough, I'll be like well, we'll go through it and we'll overcome it. Right. >> We saw you get a chance to break down the the huddle before this game. And how much does this experience drive you to want to play more? >> Thing is that my confidence level grew. Yeah. It's just a learning process for me so yeah. >> And so what's something you were able to do tonight that you weren't able to do three weeks ago? >> Like to stay clear on the field to be not not to be nervous and at least I tend to tackle. Yeah. >> Sounds like you've been asked to break down the team a few times now. Though I'm still learning the game, I just want to make an impact to keep the the team spirit together and keep going. So, I have a a zeal for more like I didn't want to the the team. So, whatever I'm asked to to break the team, I I enjoy that and I feel hyped to do that. Yeah. >> Being being an Eagle is more >> [clears throat] >> than just playing football. Obviously, during this training camp, you've gotten to see fans, fans have gotten to see you. >> What has this experience been like getting to learn Philadelphia, know Philadelphia, and interacting with the people of Philadelphia? >> So, most of most of the inspiration is my story because the fans are inspired by my story, how I came from not knowing football from Nigeria to this point to like I have a lot lot of love from the fans of me even trying to fit in and just uh three uh three plays in training camp. >> What do you think the most unexpected part of this whole experience has been for you? >> Uh I mean, the whole crowd around like like the first day I got into the stadium, it was like, man, I can't do that, but I had [snorts] the confidence to just go do my thing. >> What's the the favorite comment that you've gotten from somebody back home, you know, a family member, trainer, or whoever it may be that that really sticks with you? >> Yeah, my my coach back home always encouraged me to to keep going. So, that move me a lot. So, whenever I'm down even coach Green do tell me that. So, I don't really have any issue with that. >> Thank you for watching. Thank you. I appreciate it.
